THE TRAVELER — a passage
Sohrab Sepehri (1966)
A new English translation for this experience

The traveler’s gaze fell to the earth:
“What beautiful apples!
Life is the rapture of solitude.”
And the host asked:
“What does beautiful mean?”
“Beautiful means a loving interpretation of forms.”

And love, only love, brings you close to the warmth of an apple.
And love, only love,
carried me into the vast sorrow of lives,
brought me to the possibility of becoming a bird.
“And do you drink sorrow?”
“This draught rings with the pure note of an elixir.”

And now it was night.
The lamp was lit.
And they were drinking tea.
“Why is your heart so heavy, as though you were alone?”
“How very alone!”

“I think
you are caught in that hidden vein of colors.”
“Caught means…”
“In love.”
“And think how lonely
a little fish must be, caught in love
with the blue of the boundless sea.”

“What a tender, sorrowful thought!”
“And sorrow is the veiled smile in a plant’s gaze.
And sorrow is a faint gesture
toward the trace of the oneness of things.”

“How fortunate the plants, in love with light,
with light’s outstretched hand upon their shoulders.”
“No, union is not possible.
There is always a distance.”

Though the curve of water is a good pillow
for the water lily’s delicate, enchanting sleep,
there is always a distance.
One must be caught in love,
or the murmur of life between two letters
will be squandered.

And love
is a journey into the brightness
of the trembling solitude of things.
And love
is the sound of distances.
The sound of distances that…
“Are steeped in mystery.”

“No.
The sound of distances that are clear as silver,
and are tarnished by hearing the slightest nothing.”
The lover is always alone.
And the lover’s hand rests
in the fragile hand of seconds.

And the lover and the seconds
travel to the other side of day.
And the lover and the seconds
lie down upon the light.
And the lover and the seconds
give the finest book in the world to the water.

And they know well
that no fish has ever
unraveled the river’s
thousand and one knots.
